FN-G37SRC2-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 92
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Senator Donnie Chesteen
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/24/2025
Senate Bill 92 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of: (1) the local
boards of education to adopt policies, by July 1, 2026, relating to the use of electronic
communication devices on public school campuses and internet safety, and to provide to all
students in grades 8th - 12th the social media safety course developed and approved by the State
Department of Education; and (2) the State Department of Education to develop and approve an
online course to students regarding the use of social media. Additionally, this bill could increase
the administrative obligations of the State Board of Education to adopt rules.

FN-G37SRC2-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 92
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Senator Donnie Chesteen
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/26/2025
Senate Bill 92 as reported by the Committee on Education Policy would increase the
administrative obligations of: (1) the local boards of education to adopt policies, by July 1,
2025, relating to the use of electronic communication devices on public school campuses and
internet safety, and to provide to all students in grades 8th - 12th the social media safety course
developed and approved by the State Department of Education; (2) the State Department of
Education to develop and approve an online course for students regarding the use of social
media; and (3) the State Department of Education to develop a survey to assess participation and
compliance with wireless communication policies and to receive responses from local principals
and post the information on a public website of the department.
Additionally, this bill would reduce the common purchase allocation provided from the
Foundation Program Fund by 30% for a school that fails to meet the minimum standard of
compliance as provided in this bill. For FY 2025 the Common Purchase Allocation is $100 per
teacher unit. Finally, this bill could increase the administrative obligations of the State Board of
Education to adopt rules pursuant to the provisions of this bill.

FN-G37SRC2-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 92
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Senator Donnie Chesteen
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/14/2025
Senate Bill 92 as passed the Senate would increase the administrative obligations of: (1) the
State Department of Education to develop and approve an online course for students regarding
the use of social media and to develop a survey of teachers to assess participation and
compliance with wireless communication policies and to post the information on a public
website of the department and (2) the local boards of education to adopt policies, by July 1,
2025, relating to the use of electronic communication devices on public school campuses and
internet safety, and to provide the social media safety course to all students prior to entering 8th
grade.
Additionally, this bill could increase the administrative obligations of the State Board of
Education to adopt rules pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
